chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya from al-'Ala' ibn Razin said:

One of the two Imams (peace be upon them) was asked about a dirty garment, whether the person in ihram may wear it. He said, 'No, and I do not say it is forbidden, but purifying it is more pleasing to me, and its purification is washing it.' And if the garment had been affected by perfume, there is no harm in wearing it after its scent has gone. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامُ: Ihram, the ritual state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Is it forbidden for a pilgrim in ihram to wear a dirty or perfumed garment?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Imam (peace be upon him) clarifies the juristic distinction between prohibition and preference regarding impure garments during ihram, emphasizing that washing is the preferred method of purification rather than a mandatory requirement. The hadith further refines the ruling on perfume, noting that garments scented with perfume are permissible to wear once the scent dissipates, reflecting the Shia scholarly focus on the removal of the scent's essence rather than the substance itself. This ruling underscores the balance between ritual purity and practical ease for the pilgrim.
